title: Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
abstract: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number $C$, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact $T=0$ stiffness determinant is the topological floor times $1+(\Torb/2π|C|)^2\le1+(\TLVP/2π|C|)^2$, where $\Torb$ and $\TLVP$ measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.
summary: This theoretical work establishes a fundamental relationship governing the superfluid stiffness in flat-band superconductors characterized by Chern bands. It proves that the stiffness is bounded by a 'topological floor,' and any deviation from this floor requires a corresponding loss of 'vortexability.' This provides a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding the superconducting properties of topological materials.
main_problem: The paper determines the zero-temperature superfluid stiffness of vortexable Chern bands when paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction.
main_result: Vortexable Chern bands are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed parameters, and their stiffness sits exactly on the topological floor if and only if the splitting defect is zero.
method: The analysis compares the exact zero-temperature stiffness determinant to a derived topological lower bound, establishing a quantitative relationship between stiffness enhancement and vortexability.
model_or_system: The system involves flat-band superconductors modeled by tight-binding bands with a Chern number C, analyzed using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) formalism.
key_observables: Superfluid Stiffness ($\det D_s(0)$), Topological Floor ($\det D_{	ext{floor}, s}(0)$), Vortexability ($	ext{Torb}, 	ext{TclLVP}$), and the ratio $R = \det D_s / \det D_{	ext{floor}, s}$.
important_parameters: Chern number $|C|$, pairing amplitude, and the splitting defect $\Sigma$.
main_assumptions: The results assume uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state; the equality to the floor requires $\Sigma = 0$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the trade-off plane showing the relationship between stiffness ratio $R$ and vortexability, forbidding an upper shaded region. Other figures test specific band models (e.g., $\Theta$ band, QWZ band) against theoretical bounds.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical relationship between stiffness and vortexability, derives the inequality $\det D_s(0) / \det D_{	ext{floor}, s}(0) = 1 + (	ext{Torb}/2\pi|C|)^2 \leq 1 + (	ext{TclLVP}/2\pi|C|)^2$, and then verifies this theorem across various physical models and lattice structures.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous, quantifiable link between topological invariants (Chern number) and macroscopic superconducting properties (superfluid stiffness) in flat-band systems, which is highly relevant for designing topological superconductors.
